newsitem.title: GERMANY: Adidas confirms U.S. baseball team deal.
newsitem.headline: Adidas confirms U.S. baseball team deal.

text.p: German sportswear maker Adidas AG on Tuesday said it had signed a marketing deal with the New York Yankees baseball team, confirming a report in the Wall Street Journal.
"We have signed an agreement for broad cooperation in marketing," an Adidas spokesman said in answer to an enquiry, declining however to give more details.
Adidas shares soared on the news, climbing 3.55 percent to 172 marks ($101) in pre-bourse IBIS trading.
The Wall Street Journal had reported that the deal with Yankees, winners of the 1996 World Series, was roughly estimated at $100 million. But the Adidas spokesman called this "pure speculation".
According to the report, Adidas beat out Fila for the contract after the rival had emerged as a potential challenger on Friday.
Under the initial agreement, Adidas was to obtain the right to make uniforms for the Yankees and to sell uniform replicas to the public, the report said.
It said there were also discussions over the possibility of incorporating Adidas' three-stripe logo on the New York team's white-and-navy home-game uniforms.

The deal is valued at more than three times the sum of any existing sponsorship agreement with an individual U.S. sports team, second only to Nike's 10-year, $200 million sponsorship of Brazil's world-champion national soccer team, the report said.
